ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AE$ is the bisector of $\angle BAC$, and $ED\parallel CA$. Given that $BE=2$, $EC=3$, and $AC=4$, what is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that \\
$\because ED\parallel CA$, \\
$\therefore \triangle BED\sim \triangle BCA$, $\angle DEA=\angle EAC$, \\
$\therefore \frac{BE}{BC}=\frac{ED}{CA}$, \\
$\because BE=2$, $EC=3$, $AC=4$, \\
$\therefore BC=5$, \\
$\therefore ED=\frac{BE\cdot CA}{BC}=\frac{8}{5}$, \\
$\because AE$ bisects $\angle BAC$, \\
$\therefore \angle EAC=\angle DAE$, \\
$\therefore \angle DAE=\angle DEA$, \\
$\therefore \triangle ADE$ is an isosceles triangle, \\
$\therefore ED=AD=\boxed{\frac{8}{5}}$.
